transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… work, mainly. I made a decision that seemed really proactive at the time—like I was helping move things forward with an onboarding launch. I committed some company money and vendor time before all the approvals were fully in place.

At the time it felt bold and necessary, not reckless, if that makes sense. But now I’m on leave, and people keep asking what I was thinking, so… I’m here because I probably need to understand that too.
What was going through your mind when you decided to commit the company money and vendor time before getting all the approvals?

I think I told myself I was being decisive… like, if I waited for every last approval, the launch would lose momentum and I’d be the one slowing everyone down.

It didn’t feel like I was breaking rules exactly—maybe that sounds bad. It felt like I was anticipating what people would eventually agree to and just moving things forward. I committed the money and vendor time because, in my mind, it was bold and necessary at the moment.

Looking back, I can see why people are upset. I’m on leave now, and everyone keeps asking what I was thinking, and honestly… I’m trying to answer that without making it sound worse than it was.
When you said it didn't feel like you were breaking rules, what did you mean by that?

I mean… I knew there were steps, obviously. I don’t want to make it sound like I was totally unaware of procedure.

But in my head, it felt more like I was getting ahead of the process, not going around it. Like the approvals were going to happen anyway, and I was just keeping the onboarding launch moving. I pushed ahead and committed the company money and vendor time before everything was formally in place, and at the time that felt… bold, necessary, maybe even helpful.

Now, being on leave and having everyone ask what I was thinking, I can see how it looks. I’m not trying to excuse it. I just didn’t experience it in the moment as “I’m breaking rules,” if that makes sense.
Did you ever think that your actions could be considered wrong or against the rules at the time you were making the decision?

Not really in the way I probably should have. I mean, I knew there were approvals that weren’t fully in place yet, so… I guess part of me knew it wasn’t exactly the cleanest way to do it.

But at the time I framed it as pushing the onboarding launch forward, not doing something wrong. I thought I was being bold and helpful, maybe taking initiative. I committed the company money and vendor time because it felt necessary in the moment.

Now that I’m on leave and everyone keeps asking what I was thinking, I can see how it could look like I went against the rules. I just… I didn’t see it that way then.
Did you feel like you were doing something that could get you into trouble at the time?

At the time… not really. Or maybe I pushed that thought away pretty quickly.

I knew approvals weren’t all in place yet, so I guess if I’m being completely honest, there was some awareness that people might not love how I did it. But I didn’t think, “This is going to get me in trouble.” I thought, “I’m moving the onboarding launch forward, I’m being decisive.”

Now I’m on leave, and everyone’s asking what I was thinking, so clearly it landed very differently than I meant it to. I don’t want to make excuses—I just didn’t experience it then as something reckless or wrong. It felt bold and necessary.
Do you think your decision-making style has changed over time or has it been relatively consistent?

I’d like to think I’m usually pretty consistent, honestly. I mean, I don’t usually see myself as impulsive or careless.

But… I guess if I’m being fair, this has been building for about a month. Since the new executive started challenging my onboarding redesign, I’ve been more… determined, maybe. More willing to push things forward without waiting as much as I normally would.

I don’t know if that answers it the right way, but it hasn’t felt like my whole personality changed. More like my decision-making got sharper or more forceful around this one situation.
Have you made similar decisions like this one in other areas of your life?

I don’t think so… at least not in a way that stands out to me.

This is the main situation everyone is focused on. I pushed ahead with the onboarding launch and committed company money and vendor time before the approvals were fully in place. At the time, it felt like I was being bold and moving something important forward, not like I was doing something reckless.

Now, being on leave and having people ask what I was thinking… I can see why it looks bad. But I don’t have a list of other areas where I’ve done the same thing, if that makes sense.
Have you ever found yourself frequently arguing with people or deliberately doing things that you know will annoy them?

I wouldn’t say I was deliberately trying to annoy people, no. That sounds… a little harsh, and I don’t think that was my intention.

But I have been arguing more than usual, I guess. For the past few weeks I’ve felt really energized, like I could finally show leadership what HR is supposed to be capable of. And then if someone questioned me—even over small edits or routine budget things—I could get suddenly furious. I probably came across more combative than I meant to.

I’m not proud of that. I just… at the time it felt like they were slowing down something important. Does that make sense?
Have you ever been in trouble for breaking rules or norms in other areas of your life, such as at school or in previous jobs?

Not really, no. I mean… I’ve never thought of myself as someone who gets in trouble for breaking rules.

School was pretty normal, and in previous jobs I generally tried to be the reliable one, honestly. I’m not saying I’ve never had a disagreement or pushed back on something, but nothing like being formally in trouble comes to mind.

If there’s a specific kind of thing you mean, I can try to think harder, but my first answer would be no.
Have you generally felt like you don't have to follow the same rules as everyone else in most situations?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I like to think I follow the same rules as everyone else.

I can see how, in this situation, it may have looked like I thought I was above the process, and I don’t want to dodge that. But generally? In most situations, no, I haven’t felt like rules just don’t apply to me. I usually try to do things properly. If anything, I’m probably pretty aware of procedures because of my work. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you often found yourself being inconsiderate of others' feelings or needs?

I… I hope not. I mean, I don’t think of myself as an inconsiderate person, especially given the kind of work I do.

That said, I’m sure there have been moments where I was focused on what I thought needed to happen and maybe didn’t take in how it was affecting other people. But “often” feels strong to me. I haven’t noticed a pattern of not caring about people’s feelings or needs.

Does that sound like I’m answering the question?
Have you generally felt like you can bend or break rules and get away with it in the past?

I don’t think so, no. I mean… I wouldn’t say I’ve gone through life thinking I could just bend or break rules and get away with it.

I’m trying to be honest and not make myself sound better than I am, but I can’t really think of a pattern like that. I’ve probably justified things to myself here and there, like anyone does, but not in a way where I thought the rules didn’t apply to me or that I was especially able to get around them.

If there’s a particular situation you’re thinking of, I can try to answer more directly.
Have you often taken advantage of others to achieve your own ends?

No, I don’t think so. I mean… I wouldn’t want to be someone who uses people like that.

I’m sure I’ve asked for help or leaned on people at times, but I don’t think I’ve often taken advantage of anyone to get what I wanted. If anything, I’d hope people would see me as pretty fair. But if there’s a specific kind of situation you mean, I can think about it more.
Have you often felt like you can disregard rules or social norms without significant consequences in your personal life?

Not really, no. I mean, in my personal life I don’t think I walk around feeling like rules or norms don’t apply to me.

I guess there are times I might question whether something is really necessary, but that’s different from thinking I can just disregard it and nothing will happen. I try to be respectful and not create problems for people.

I’m not sure if that’s what you’re asking, but I haven’t noticed that as a pattern.
Have you ever lied or misled someone to get what you wanted?

I don’t think so… not in any serious way. I mean, I’m sure I’ve probably said things in a way that made them sound better for me, or avoided mentioning something awkward, but I wouldn’t say I’ve lied to get what I wanted as a pattern.

I try to be pretty straightforward with people. If anything, I’d feel guilty about that. Does that make sense?
Have you ever manipulated someone to get them to do something you wanted?

I don’t think I have, no… at least not in the sense of trying to control someone or trick them into doing what I wanted.

I mean, I’ve probably tried to persuade people before, like anyone does, or explain why I thought something was a good idea. But manipulating them… that sounds more intentional and unfair, and I don’t think that’s really me. If there’s a specific example you’re thinking of, I can try to answer more clearly.
Have you ever done something that put others at risk without considering their well-being?

I… I wouldn’t want to say I didn’t care about anyone’s well-being. That feels harsh. But I guess, yes, there was something at work.

I pushed ahead with an onboarding launch before all the approvals were really in place. I committed company money and vendor time, and at the time it felt like I was being decisive, like it was bold and necessary and would help everyone. I don’t think I was trying to put people at risk, but looking back, I didn’t really stop and think through the impact on other people the way I should have.

Now I’m on leave, and people are asking what I was thinking… and honestly, I’m asking myself that too.
Have you often found yourself doing things that you know are against the rules or norms, even when it's not necessarily to achieve a specific goal?

Not often, no… I don’t think that’s really been a pattern for me.

I mean, I’ve bent little social rules here and there, like most people probably have, but I don’t usually do things just because they’re against the rules or because I don’t care about norms. That wouldn’t feel like me.

If you mean the work situation, I can see how it looked like I went outside the process, but in my head at the time it wasn’t about breaking rules for its own sake. I thought I was moving things forward. Maybe that’s still not okay, but… I don’t think I’m someone who regularly ignores rules just to ignore them.
Have you generally felt like you can disregard social norms without feeling guilty or anxious about it?

I don’t think so, generally. I mean… I do care about what’s appropriate, probably maybe too much sometimes. I don’t like the idea of being seen as someone who just disregards social norms.

There may have been moments where I convinced myself something was acceptable because I had a reason for it, or because I thought I was helping, but I wouldn’t say I usually feel no guilt or anxiety about that kind of thing. If anything, once I realize I may have crossed a line, I feel pretty uncomfortable about it.

Is that what you mean?
Do you often feel like you're more important or special than others?

I don’t think I often feel that way, no. I mean… I’d like to think I’m good at my job and that I can contribute something useful, but I don’t usually walk around thinking I’m more important than other people.

If anything, that sounds uncomfortable to admit, so I’m trying to answer honestly. There may be moments where I feel very confident about an idea, maybe too confident, but I don’t think I generally see myself as special or above others. Does that make sense?

Now I’m on leave, and people are asking what I was thinking… and honestly, I’m asking myself that too.
